name: issue-driven-dev
description: v3.1.0: the actionability gate, rounds 2 to 7. Round 1 read `### Complexity` against a closed value domain that the repository's own 159 diagnoses refuted (66 real values wrongly refused) and shipped a three-signal gate no consumer called. Now the tier is the leading whole word (rationale, decoration and ` via` suffixes are legal), the whole line is scanned for a small deferral vocabulary (exit 5, reason `complexity-deferral-marker` — a parked state, not a defect), and `### Blocking` is read per bullet by a shared helper with a leading-token placeholder rule frozen against the repo's 55 real rows — 54 sections under CommonMark (54/55 agree with hand review; round 2 had withheld 30 of the 48 empty ones, #316 itself among them). idd-list / idd-all / idd-implement / idd-plan call the verdict with all three signals before any branch or comment, print it as a machine line plus a delimited raw block, and repeat the gate byte for byte where a later step routes on it (pinned by test). Fences follow CommonMark's two visibility rules; the reader's known divergences from CommonMark are listed with their direction and pinned, not claimed exhaustive. The placeholder rule does not depend on the locale or on a shell function named grep; the matchers that still follow the environment are listed with their measured directions (#336). Changes to the reader are gated: vocabulary rules move only toward withholding unless a named corpus row requires the change; structural rules (headings, fences, bullets, trimming, and the locale of their matchers) are frozen until a requirement names the oracle they converge on (#336). idd-list gains Parked and Needs-diagnosis groups; the #84 blocked surface is preserved verbatim.
